best_for: People with several computers or a home server who want folders kept in sync directly between their own devices instead of through a cloud account.
description:
Syncthing is a free, open source program that keeps folders the same on two or more computers, updating them as files change. It is made by the Syncthing Authors, and the protocol it uses to talk between devices is published as an open, documented specification.

Each machine has a device ID. You swap IDs with a friend, or between your own computers, pick a folder to share, and files start moving over your home network or the internet, with no IP addresses to type. If you cannot forward ports on your router, it can open them through UPnP. You can share as many folders as you like, each with different people, or sync your desktops with a home server to keep a backup copy.

points.title: No cloud in the middle
points.text: Files live only on your own devices. Connections use TLS with forward secrecy, each device has its own certificate, and only devices you approve can connect.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Syncthing is free under MPL-2.0. The project takes donations, and paid support is available from Kastelo for companies that want it.

points.title: Set up in a browser
points.text: You add folders and devices through a web page that Syncthing serves locally. The core program is a background service without its own window.

points.title: The Windows zip is the bare program
points.text: The Windows entries here are the base zip for x86, x64 and ARM64. It has no tray icon or autostart. For that, Syncthing's site lists Syncthing Windows Setup and SyncTrayzor as separate integrations.

points.title: Mac gets an app
points.text: The Mac entry is a universal .dmg app for macOS 12 or later. On Syncthing's site the Mac app bundle is listed as an integration with its own issue tracker, apart from the base zip.

points.title: Versions kept
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 52 versions; macOS lists only the current release, which at review time was 2.1.6-1 against 2.1.7 on Windows.
